reviewers: Primary agent: pose, profile, mobile and unpaused playback sample review
Peer agent: all eight peak portraits, surprise profile, source wording and live scene review
Model author: repeated silhouette, surface, aperture and profile corrections

scope.method: Reviewed rendered six-pose sequences, all eight front and profile peaks, mobile wink and surprise layouts, and seven screenshots from uninterrupted playback of each expression across a loop boundary. The final wink closure was inspected again after its targeted repair. Sampled visual review is not continuous frame-by-frame or clinical validation.

repairs: Smoothed adaptive facial surface normals and removed visible shading bands.
Refined the crown, brow orientation, eye rims, chin and hair silhouette.
Deformed the rear jaw shell and upper neck with the front face to close the profile gap during jaw opening.
Recessed and smoothed the dental arc; hid it for the rounded surprise aperture.
Repaired the fully closed wink boundary with a joined lid surface and clean crease.
Balanced portrait lighting and framed the portrait consistently in desktop, mobile, front and profile views.
Measured actual eyelid aperture and visibility; labeled jaw movement as an authored release percentage.

studies.observations: Mouth corners and cheeks lift together; the eyes soften and the dental arc stays behind the lips.
The inner brows lift, the lids lower, and the mouth corners descend without changing the portrait identity.
The brows draw inward while the eyes narrow and the lips press into a firmer line.
Wide eyelids and a stretched mouth separate the expression from surprise.
The rounded mouth opening and raised brows remain readable from the front and profile; the jaw remains connected to the back of the head.
An asymmetric upper-lip and nose lift provide a distinct acting pose.
One eyelid closes completely with a clean crease, its iris disappears, and the other eye remains open. Both eyes recover at the loop boundary.
The jaw opens more broadly than joy, with raised cheeks, narrowing eyes and a slight head lift.

limitations: An original stylized adult woman, not a scanned or photorealistic portrait.
Expression presets are authored acting interpretations, not emotion recognition or diagnostic facial analysis.
Surface deformations illustrate feature coordination; they do not simulate individual biological muscle fibers.
